metadata.title: Correct the import-time data root in Beagle and the fixed trusted root in gitUpper
metadata.author: Claude Opus 5

language-rules.rule: Write all prose in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
Use the imperative mood for each instruction.
Write one instruction in one sentence.
Keep procedural sentences to 20 words or fewer.
Use one word for one meaning.
Do not use an abbreviation before you define it.
Verify the prose with vale. Do not verify the prose by eye.

notation.description: This directive states each behaviour as a propositional expression. Each expression has a legend. The legend defines every identifier. Use one notation in one block. Do not mix the symbols.

defect.title: The instance RAG root binds at import time and defeats test isolation

evidence.observation: The module computes the root when Python imports the module. The statement is `_INSTANCE_RAG_ROOT = str(get_data_root() / "instance_rag")`.
`get_data_root()` reads the `BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT` environment variable. A test that sets this variable after the import gets the live root.
The production store held 2 chunks on 2026-08-29. Both chunks came from `/tmp/pytest-of-server/`. No real repository was present in the store.
`rag_search` returned a unit-test fixture for the query "fan control PWM curve". The distance was 0.545. The result was confident and wrong.
The docstring of `db_root()` promises call-time resolution. The module-level constants do not keep this promise.

current-behaviour.logic:
R(t_c) = g(E(t_i))
where: t_i = the time when Python imports rag_paths t_c = the time when a caller reads the root E(t) = the value of BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT at time t g(e) = the root that get_data_root() derives from e R(t_c) = the instance RAG root that the caller receives
current-behaviour.consequence: A change of the environment variable after `t_i` has no effect. The test writes to the production store.

required-behaviour.logic:
∀ t_c : t_c ≥ t_i ⇒ R(t_c) = g(E(t_c))
where: t_i = the time when Python imports rag_paths t_c = the time when a caller reads the root E(t) = the value of BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT at time t g(e) = the root that get_data_root() derives from e R(t_c) = the instance RAG root that the caller receives

isolated(T) ⇔ ∀ w ∈ W(T) : within(w, D(T))
where: T = one test W(T) = the set of file writes that T makes D(T) = the directory that BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT names while T runs within(w,d)= w resolves inside d isolated(T)= T writes no data outside its own directory
required-behaviour.constraint: Compute `within` with real path resolution. Use `Path.relative_to` on resolved paths. Do not compare string prefixes, because a symbolic link defeats a prefix test.

instructions.step: Replace the module-level constants with functions that resolve at call time.
Return the same type as before, which is `str`.
Find every reader of the old constants. Use `graph_callers` from Beagle.
Repoint each reader at the function.
Add a test that sets BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT after the import and asserts the new root.
Add a test that asserts no write goes to the home directory store.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not delete the production store to make a test pass.
Do not add a cache that restores the import-time behaviour.
Do not mark the failing test as expected, skipped, or extra-slow.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: A test sets BEAGLE_DATA_ROOT after the import. The root changes.
A full test run does not change `~/.beagle/instance_rag`. Record the chunk count before the run and after the run. The two counts are equal.
`rag_status` reports the same `indexed_chunks` before and after the test run.

defect.title: The gitUpper MCP surface cannot reach a repository outside its own project root

evidence.observation: `_default_trusted_root()` walks up from the current directory of the server process. It looks for a project marker.
The server takes its current directory from the client at start. The trusted root therefore depends on where the client started.
`get_status` refused `/home/server/.config/beagle` on 2026-08-29. `get_status` also refused `/home/server/.claude`. The error was "path is outside the allowed project workspace".
The `project_root` parameter did not change the result. Both parameters reach the same containment test.
The configuration has no key for a trusted root. An operator cannot correct this without a change to the code.

current-behaviour.logic:
allowed(p) ⇔ contained(p, d(c))
where: p = the path that the caller supplies c = the current directory of the MCP server process d(c) = the nearest ancestor of c that holds a project marker contained(x,r) = x resolves inside r allowed(p) = the server accepts p
current-behaviour.consequence: The set of reachable repositories has exactly one member. An operator cannot extend the set.

required-behaviour.logic:
valid(r) ⇔ absolute(r) ∧ directory(r) ∧ ¬broad(r)
broad(r) ⇔ r ∈ { /, /home, /usr, /etc, /var, /opt } ∨ depth(r) < 2
where: r = one candidate trusted root absolute(r)= r starts at the file system root directory(r) = r exists and is a directory depth(r) = the count of path components in r broad(r) = r gives access to too much of the file system valid(r) = the server accepts r as a trusted root

C = ∅ ⇒ ( allowed(p) ⇔ contained(p, d(c)) )
where: C = the roots that config.toml declares ∅ = the empty set p = the path that the caller supplies c = the current directory of the MCP server process d(c) = the nearest ancestor of c that holds a project marker contained(x,r) = x resolves inside r allowed(p) = the server accepts p
required-behaviour.constraint: The last expression states the compatibility rule. An operator who declares no root keeps the present behaviour. The change is therefore fail-closed by default.
Reject an invalid root at the time the server reads the configuration. Write a warning to the log. Do not stop the server.
Keep the error message for the caller unchanged. The message must not show a trusted root, because that leaks the layout.

instructions.step: Add a `trusted_roots` key to the security section of the configuration schema.
Give the key an empty list as its default value.
Expand `~` and environment variables in each entry.
Test each entry against `valid(r)`. Discard an entry that fails. Log the reason.
Pass the accepted roots to `assert_path_contained` as `trusted_roots`.
Keep the derived root in the set, so present callers continue to work.
Add a test for a path inside a declared root. The server accepts the path.
Add a test for a path outside every root. The server refuses the path.
Add a test for a symbolic link that points outside every root. The server refuses the path.
Add a test for an empty configuration. The behaviour equals the present behaviour.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not remove the containment test.
Do not use a string prefix to test containment.
Do not make the default configuration accept the home directory.
Do not show a trusted root in an error that a caller receives.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: A declared root permits `get_status` on a repository inside that root.
A path outside every root gets the unchanged error message.
A symbolic link that leaves a trusted root does not pass the test.
An empty `trusted_roots` list gives the behaviour of the present release.

global-constraints.constraint: Correct the cause. Do not hide the symptom. A broken feature is a defect to correct, not a feature to disable.
Do not disable a lint rule. A lint result shows a defect in the input.
Change only the files that these two defects name. Do not change the format of other code.
Give each public function a Google-style docstring. Include the `Args:`, `Returns:` and `Raises:` sections.
Mark each rule that must not change with an `<invariant>` comment.
Cite a file and a line for each claim about the code. Read the line before you cite it.
Each of the two repositories takes its own commit. Do not put both corrections in one commit.

verification.description: Run the gate through routeUpper. Do not start a sibling tool from the shell. Report the output of the gate. A statement that the code "should work" is not a verification.
verification.gate-condition:
complete ⇔ L ∧ T ∧ A ∧ ¬S
where: L = the quality gate reports zero violations T = every test passes A = every acceptance criterion has evidence S = a test was skipped, deselected, or marked as expected to fail complete = the work is ready for a commit

output-contract.item: A unified diff for each repository.
The output of the quality gate for each repository.
The output of the test run for each repository.
One line for each acceptance criterion, with the command that proves it.
A list of every file that you changed, with the reason.
A statement of any criterion that you could not meet, with the reason.

escalation.rule: Retry a failed tool call one time. Report the error after the second failure.
Stop after three review cycles. Report the disagreement to the user.
Ask the user before you change the default security behaviour of gitUpper.
